jobs.description:
Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture

Who We Are

Teranet is Canada’s leader in the delivery and transformation of statutory registry services with extensive expertise in land and commercial registries. We also market insightful property and data solutions, as well as practice management automation to thousands of customers in the real estate, financial services, government, utilities, and legal markets.

Connect. Grow. Thrive Together.

To learn more about who we are visit our website: www.teranet.ca

About the Role

Teranet’s diverse businesses are complex and require healthy architectural oversight to ensure alignment of the technology solutions with the business strategy. This role will have a portfolio of responsibilities related to architecture, strategy, and planning, and will have oversight of the activities of several very senior and experienced technical leaders.

The Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture is accountable for owning and driving architectural solutions across the enterprise, inclusive of line-of-business (LOB), Enterprise IT, and corporate solutions. This role drives the creation and adoption of Teranet’s multi-year IT roadmap. The IT roadmap drives multi-year IT investment decisions and broadly impacts technology spending of ~ $25M (excludes people costs) per year to deliver business value across the enterprise.

All system, technology, and solution architects in Teranet, across the enterprise, will report to this role. As such, this position will have a widespread impact on the business capabilities delivered in partnership with the Registry & Property Solutions, Financial Solutions, Enterprise IT, Information Security, and other departments at Teranet.

Reason for Vacancy: Net New Role

What You’ll Be Doing

Develop IT strategy that maintains alignment between business and IT and which will drive
multi-year IT investment decisions.
Contribute to the development of the company’s strategic roadmap.
Lead Teranet’s enterprise-wide IT roadmap, defining the future-state architecture and transformation of technology, people, organizational design, and processes.
Contribute to the execution of digital transformation efforts.
Define the technology solution and environment roadmaps to ensure capacity and scalability as demand and usage evolve within the business.
Have visibility and understanding of the entire technology landscape.
Identify, assess, and communicate risks related to the roadmaps, to strategic IT initiatives, and to Teranet’s business from emerging technology trends.
Participate, as required, in executive- and board-level discussions on technology and strategy.

Manage a team of architects responsible for creating technology solutions to business problems, developing new business capabilities, and providing technical direction to implementation teams.

Mentor and manage team members to achieve program targets and goals.
Hold direct accountability for all technology and data architects across the enterprise.
Oversee the time management, prioritization, and effectiveness of all team members.
Evaluate team members on their achievement of goals.
Ensure development, coaching, and mentoring plans are in place for all team members.
Prepare and track the budget and forecast for the Enterprise Architecture team.

Govern the practice of architecture at Teranet. Develop principles, processes, and standards and ensure adherence to same.

Chair the architecture board responsible for reviewing and approving architecture, technology, and design decisions across the enterprise.
Partner closely with and maintain regular touchpoints with key partners, including product development, customers, finance, PMO, vendors, and delivery teams.
Manage the allocation of architecture resources to various initiatives.
Create and communicate solutions to various business problems.
Oversee adherence to the architecture strategy, principles, and framework throughout IT.
Lead the definition and validation of architecture principles and standards.
Ensure systems are architected to be secure and resilient through the effective application of architecture principles across the domains of Business, Application, Data, Integration, Technology/Infrastructure, and Security.
Communicate architecture standards to all stakeholders and ensure standards are published, updated, and followed.
Communicate the impacts, trade-offs, risks, costs, benefits, and opportunities of IT decisions as needed.
Stay current on architecture, IT strategy, and technology innovation best practices and trends.
Define and track architecture KPIs/metrics, including standards compliance, technical debt reduction, and reuse rates.

Contribute to the success of M&A activitythrough deep understanding of the business and involvement in most stages of the M&A lifecycle.

Perform technology due diligence.
Evaluate acquisitions for ability to integrate with Teranet and ensure acquisitions include adequate integration funding to (a) realize immediate value and (b) realize efficiencies.
Lead the IT team as it influences the outcome of mergers and acquisitions, ensuring that IT needs are considered and supporting the M&A efforts during and following the deal.

What You Bring:

Bachelor’s degree with 10+ years of progressive leadership and IT experience.
Experience in large, sophisticated organizations.
Demonstrated experience in managing an organization’s complex technology plans.
Demonstrated experience in cross-group coordination across a wide range of management levels and functional disciplines.
Demonstrated experience in developing and supporting mission critical applications.
Exhibited deep knowledge of system architecture, technical design, system and software development technology.
Demonstrated track record of disseminating new insights, changes, and processes across complex and matrixed organizations.
Experience in the real estate and/or financial services industries is an asset.
Technical expertise coupled with an understanding of business principles.
Direct experience leading architecture for major transformation programs, including AI, automation, cloud, and infrastructure initiatives.
Strong knowledge of modern architecture patterns, including microservices, API-led integration, cloud-native, and event-driven architecture.
Experience working within multiple project/SDLC methodologies, including Agile/Scrum and SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework).
TOGAF certification (or equivalent enterprise architecture certification) preferred; SAFe certification (e.g., SPC, ARC) a plus.

Agility/Capability/Leadership

Strong knowledge of emerging digital technologies, including cloud, SaaS/PaaS, APIs, mobile, AI and machine learning, with experience across platforms such as AWS, Azure or GCP.
Demonstrated ability to identify, assess and leverage emerging technologies to drive innovation, business value and competitive advantage.
Experience with modern DevOps, platform engineering and AI/ML architecture practices, including responsible AI and governance considerations.
Strong business and technology acumen, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts and opportunities into clear business terms.
Proven leadership experience building, developing, motivating and inspiring high-performing teams while fostering transparency, accountability and shared purpose.
Strong executive presence, communication and influencing skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across technical, business and senior leadership teams.
Demonstrated ability to lead change, establish priorities, remove barriers and drive results in complex and fast-paced environments.
Strong critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience navigating large-scale technology environments and ambiguous situations.
A collaborative and authentic leader who demonstrates empathy, strong listening skills, sound judgment and effective conflict resolution.
Results-oriented, adaptable and highly motivated, with the ability to remain calm, focused and decisive through change and uncertainty.

What We Offer

100% Employer Paid Health Benefit Plan
Employer Matching Retirement Savings Plan
Paid Vacation, Floater Days & Sick Leaves
Maternity, Parental and/or Adoption Leave Top-Up Programs
Corporate Discounts & GoodLife Group Rate Membership

jobs.title: Director, Technology, Campana Systems
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Aquila, we invest in category-defining B2B/B2G software companies globally, acting as a thought-partner, striving for the success of our companies in the long term. We are a well-managed, profitable company that operates like a startup with the financial backing of a parent company. For our people, this means limitless possibilities.

We are unapologetically unique, pivoting to respond to the needs of the multiple markets we operate in. We have ambitious goals, and we are looking for genuine contributors with integrity, energy, flexibility, and loyalty. We are investing in building future leaders who can take an idea and make things happen.

About Campana Systems

Campana Systems, a Gemini Group company within Aquila, develops specialized software solutions for AAA and CAA auto clubs across North America. Founded in 1988 and headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, Campana has built long-standing relationships with organizations that rely on its technology to manage their operations and deliver services to their members.

Our AXIS platform brings together membership management, customer relationship management, emergency roadside assistance, travel services, and business intelligence in an integrated suite of solutions. Looking ahead, we are focused on evolving our technology, strengthening our platform capabilities, and finding new ways to help our customers work more efficiently and deliver better member experiences.

Who we need

Reporting to the General Manager, we are hiring a Director, Technology to lead the evolution of Campana Systems’ technology strategy, architecture, infrastructure, and AXIS platform. In this newly created role, you will own the technology roadmap from strategy through execution, with accountability for modernization priorities, investment decisions, platform reliability, and measurable business outcomes. You will lead the Architecture and Infrastructure & Security teams, partner with the Director, Development, and establish the technical direction and capabilities needed to deliver on our product vision while supporting the customers who depend on our technology.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates across Canada, with working hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time.

What’s in it for you

Shape a meaningful transformation . You will have the autonomy to challenge established approaches, make consequential technology decisions, and guide the evolution of a business-critical software platform. You will see the impact of your work in stronger platform capabilities, improved delivery, and better customer experiences.

Build what comes next. You will lead experienced teams while shaping the standards, capabilities, and ways of working needed for the future. From strengthening engineering practices to developing technical leaders, you will have the opportunity to build a more effective technology organization and see the results of your leadership.

Grow your executive influence. You will work directly with the General Manager and contribute to decisions that connect technology investments with customer needs and business growth. Backed by Aquila and the broader Constellation Software network, you will have opportunities to expand your leadership experience and pursue broader responsibilities over time.

As our new Director, Technology, you will

Own the technology roadmap
. You will turn the product vision into a multi-year strategy with clear priorities, investments, milestones, and measurable outcomes. You will balance modernization, technical debt, customer commitments, and platform stability, taking accountability for delivery and results. You will establish architectural standards, technology governance, and engineering priorities. Partnering with the Director, Development, you will strengthen technical decision-making, CI/CD, automation, and delivery practices across Canadian and offshore teams.
Lead platform modernization.
You will define a phased approach to evolving AXIS, including its legacy Rocket UniVerse architecture. You will determine what to retain, integrate, replace, or modernize, guiding decisions on APIs, application architecture, CRM, data capabilities, and cloud or hybrid environments while protecting the reliability customers depend on.
Turn innovation into impact.
You will identify opportunities to improve CRM capabilities, business intelligence, reporting, and operational efficiency through AI, automation, and better use of data. You will evaluate feasibility and business value, establish priorities, and work with technical teams to turn promising initiatives into measurable results.
Strengthen security and reliability.
You will oversee infrastructure, hosting, cybersecurity, disaster recovery, and platform resilience. You will reduce technology risk, strengthen operational controls, and advance security and compliance readiness, including SOC 2-related requirements.
Build and grow technical capabilities.
You will lead the Architecture and Infrastructure & Security teams, develop talent, strengthen accountability, and identify capability gaps. You will improve collaboration with Development and Product to ensure teams have the direction and support needed to execute the roadmap.
Connect technology to business priorities.
You will partner with the General Manager on technology investments, budgets, resources, and strategic decisions. You will communicate risks and trade-offs, measure progress, and contribute technical leadership to customer conversations when needed.

You bring

The senior technology leadership.
You have led technology strategy, architecture, and technical teams within an enterprise software business, with accountability for investment decisions, organizational performance, and business outcomes. You bring the judgment to set direction, establish priorities, and deliver results through technical leaders and cross-functional teams.
The platform modernization expertise.
You have led the evolution of complex, business-critical software, navigating legacy architecture, technical debt, and customer dependencies. You know how to assess what to retain, replace, or integrate, develop a phased modernization roadmap, and introduce new capabilities without compromising reliability.
The technical depth.
You bring strong expertise in enterprise architecture, APIs, integrations, data platforms, and cloud or hybrid environments, along with an understanding of infrastructure, cybersecurity, and disaster recovery. You can establish technical standards, evaluate emerging technologies, and guide decisions that strengthen platform performance, security, and scalability.
The experience driving innovation.
You have improved engineering practices and delivery performance across distributed teams, including those outside your direct reporting structure. You understand CI/CD, automation, and modern development practices, and can identify practical opportunities for AI, analytics, and business intelligence that deliver measurable value.
The business acumen.
You connect technology decisions to customer needs, financial priorities, and long-term business growth. You can evaluate investments, communicate complex trade-offs, and align senior leaders while staying close enough to the technology to challenge assumptions and guide execution.
The influence.
You develop strong technical leaders, establish accountability, and build cross-functional, cross-location collaboration. You are comfortable making difficult decisions, navigating competing priorities, and owning outcomes in an environment where you have the autonomy to shape what comes next.

Why join?

Axis Campana and Aquila are part of Constellation Software Inc., one of Canada's largest and most successful software companies and its most successful technology stock over the last 10 years [TSE: CSU].

Our entrepreneurial culture, lean environment, and people come together to form a dynamic organization where purpose drives our growth. This is a place where high performance and hard work are rewarded, where leaders are grown, and where the best ideas win. With the autonomy to be creative and curious, we collaborate and iterate to achieve real impact in the communities we support.

We spend our days asking questions and challenging the status quo, manipulating our structure, roles, and internal operations in order to stay ahead in a competitive landscape.

If you share our growth mindset, relationship-focused approach, and high moral fibre, you will thrive at Aquila.

Compensation

At Campana and Aquila, we believe compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of both experience and impact. The salary range for this role is CAD $150,000 to $200,000 plus bonus.

Compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and the scope and complexity of the role. We value open conversations about compensation and are happy to discuss our approach at any stage of the hiring process.

Apply now.

Diversity and inclusion are not mere words on paper to us. We welcome and appreciate candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you have most of the qualifications we are seeking, and want to play an integral role in our success, apply to express your interest.

What you can expect from our interview process:

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining the company and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An interview with the General Manager to discuss your technology leadership experience, approach to platform modernization, architectural decision-making, and ability to connect technology strategy to business outcomes.
A final virtual interview with the Portfolio Manager and members of the technology leadership team to explore your approach to leading transformation, collaborating across teams, and building the capabilities needed to execute the technology roadmap.

Aquila and Campana Systems promote equal employment opportunities for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, national origin, veteran status, marital status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and accommodations are available on request.

The President & Vice Chancellor
(“President”), serving as the CEO, is responsible for the leadership and general management of the affairs of KPU in accordance with provincial legislation and policies, and strategy set by the Board. The President articulates a direction that is congruent with the KPU’s mission, vision, values, and goals in furthering its academic standards and fulfilling its role as a polytechnic university in the community. The President provides strategic, visionary, informed, and effective leadership and decision-making in a complex, multi-faceted, and public context. The President ensures materials are available for Board activities and participates in the essential functions of the Board, including governance, compliance, and policy formulation.

KPU is at a critical stage in its evolution; coming on the heels of a decade of growth and change, KPU’s next President will lead an institution which has leveraged the considerable talents of its communities to innovate, raise its profile, rebuild its infrastructure, and solidify its partnerships, but must also work through the pressures connected with declining international student enrolment. KPU must remain agile, at the vanguard of change, with a President who understands how education will prepare tomorrow’s workforce and global citizens.

This is an outstanding opportunity for a dynamic leader to take KPU to the next level. Balancing the responsibilities of external relationships and internal stewardship, the President should be accessible and transparent, and able to find the common purpose amongst the institution’s many communities. With an increased focus on reconciliation and decolonization; anti-racism; justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion; and environmental sustainability, the President will know how to put these ideas into meaningful action in order to create an institution that welcomes and supports all learners.
